turns.t: Hi, are you Dan? Take a seat, the doctor's running five minutes behind. I've just updated your student details. ~
Cool. Can we hurry it up? I've got a lecture at two and I'm already behind. ~
Hello Dan, I'm Dr Okafor. I'll be quick but thorough. What's brought you in? ~
I'm knackered. I had a bad flu in October, and I've never really got over it. It's been six weeks.
What does knackered feel like?
Like my battery's at ten percent. I sleep nine hours and wake up tired. I can't concentrate in lectures.
Any other symptoms?
My throat's been sore on and off, and my glands feel lumpy, here.
Any fever, night sweats, or weight loss?
No fever. I'd have noticed.
How's your university life? Sleep, stress, workload? ~
I'm doing a double module and a part-time job at the bar. So, not much downtime. ~
That's a lot. Have you been in contact with anyone with glandular fever? ~
My housemate had it last month. ~
That's interesting, and relevant. ~
Do you think I've got it? ~
I can't rule out glandular fever, given your housemate, the sore throat, the tender glands, and fatigue after a viral illness, though it could also be a slow recovery from the flu.
Can you test for it? ~
Yes, I'd like to arrange a blood test, to check for the glandular fever virus and your blood count.
I can book that in for you now, Dan, at the front desk. ~
Fine. Does it hurt? ~
Just a quick scratch. ~
In the meantime, no contact sports, in case your spleen is enlarged, and avoid alcohol until we know.
No alcohol, that'll be hard in Freshers' week. ~
It's not Freshers' week, Dan. ~
Ha, no. But the bar job. ~
Maybe ask for shifts that don't involve lifting crates, too. Rest when you can, and eat regularly.
Right. ~
If you get severe tummy pain on the left side, or a high fever, or difficulty swallowing, come in the same day.
Okay, okay. Thanks, doc. ~
